temas.tema: Remote work and the future of offices
perguntas: Do you work from home, from an office, or both? Which do you prefer?
What is the worst part of commuting in your city?
What do you miss when you don't see your colleagues?
How do you avoid distractions when you work at home?
Do you think people work more or less at home? Why?
What makes a good home office?
How has your routine changed since remote work became common?
Would you accept a lower salary to work from home? Why?
How do you keep in touch with colleagues you never meet?
What jobs can never be done remotely?
aprofundar: Some companies are forcing people back to the office. Is that about productivity or control?
How does remote work affect young professionals who are just starting their careers?
What happens to city centers if offices stay empty?
Can company culture exist without a physical space?
Who benefits most from remote work: employees or employers?
How should remote workers be evaluated — by hours or by results?
debate: Companies should let employees choose where they work.
Remote work is making people lonelier.

roleplay.situacao: You want to work from home three days a week. Convince your manager (the teacher), who prefers the office.

temas.escrita: Write a short email (100–150 words) to your manager asking for a hybrid schedule. Give two reasons and one guarantee.

perguntas: How many hours a day do you think you use your phone?
What app do you open first in the morning?
Do notifications distract you? What do you do about it?
Have you ever tried a digital detox? How was it?
What did you do in your free time before smartphones?
Do you think children should have phones? From what age?
What technology could you never live without?
Is there an app you deleted because it was wasting your time?
Do you prefer reading on paper or on a screen?
How do you feel when you forget your phone at home?
aprofundar: Are tech companies responsible for our addiction to their apps?
Should schools ban phones completely?
Is it possible to be successful today without social media?
How is technology changing the way we remember things?
Does constant access to information make us smarter or more superficial?
What rules do you think families should have about screens?
debate: Social media does more harm than good.
Phones should be banned in schools.

roleplay.situacao: Convince a family member (the teacher) to accept a no-phones rule at dinner.
roleplay.papeis: Aluno: quem propõe a regra · Professor: adolescente que não quer

temas.escrita: Describe your relationship with your phone in one paragraph. What would you like to change?

Is traveling necessary to understand other cultures, or can books and films do it?
How has social media changed the way people travel?
What's the difference between a tourist and a traveler?
Is it ethical to fly often, considering climate change?

Traveling alone is better than traveling with friends.

roleplay.papeis: Aluno: passageiro · Professor: atendente pouco prestativo

roleplay.situacao: Your reservation is not in the system. Solve it politely but firmly.

temas.escrita: Write a review (120 words) of a place you visited, with one thing you loved and one thing to improve.

perguntas: What do you do to stay healthy?
How many hours do you usually sleep?

Is it easy to eat well in your routine? Why?
What is the most stressful part of your week?
Do you take breaks during work? How?

Is the fitness culture on social media healthy or harmful?
Why is it so hard to change habits, even when we know they're bad?
Should unhealthy food be taxed?
Is burnout a personal problem or a social problem?
How much should the government interfere in people's health choices?

Companies should offer a four-day week for mental health.

roleplay.situacao: Explain your symptoms (tiredness, headaches) and ask questions about the treatment.

temas.escrita: Write about one habit you want to change: why, how, and how you'll measure progress.

Does money bring happiness after a certain point?
